data.narrative:
Canada Rocket Company is a seed-stage space & aerospace developer founded by Hugh Kolias and David Tenny that has raised $6.2M to date. The valuation universe comprises five public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and eight private peers including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable method given data constraints. Using total raised ($6.2M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $15.5M. This produces a range of $13M (low) to $18M (high), centered on $16M. Peer-median triangulation could not be applied: while 11 same-sector private peers exist, none satisfy narrow filtering for same or adjacent stage with comparable valuation tier. Public-comp P/S anchoring is inapplicable because the target's revenue is not disclosed, a standard constraint for private companies. The public sector median of 23.9x P/S across the five tickers provides limited utility absent revenue data.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $13M–$18M, with a central estimate of $16M. Primary uncertainty stems from reliance on a single method and the absence of revenue visibility; early-stage space ventures often exhibit wide variance in capital deployment efficiency and technical execution risk. A subsequent financing round or revenue traction would materially improve valuation precision.
